#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""check_pg_standby_lag.py - replay lag of a PostgreSQL hot standby, in seconds.

Connects to the PostgreSQL server on the machine the plugin runs on: PGHOST defaults to the
local socket directory /var/run/postgresql, and there is no --host flag. Schedule the
service on the standby's own Icinga agent (command_endpoint = the database host). Run anywhere
else, it reads whichever PostgreSQL happens to be local there.

If the server it reaches is not in recovery (pg_is_in_recovery() returns false: a primary or a
standalone server), there is no replay to fall behind, so the plugin reports 0 s and exits OK.
It prints nothing to say that this happened.
"""
import os
import sys

import psycopg2

PGHOST = os.environ.get("PGHOST", "/var/run/postgresql")
WARN_S = 60
CRIT_S = 300


def replay_lag(conn):
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("SELECT pg_is_in_recovery()")
    if not cur.fetchone()[0]:
        return 0
    cur.execute("SELECT COALESCE(date_part('epoch', now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp()), 0)")
    return int(cur.fetchone()[0])


def main():
    conn = psycopg2.connect(host=PGHOST, dbname="postgres", user="nagios")
    lag = replay_lag(conn)
    perf = f"replay_lag={lag}s;{WARN_S};{CRIT_S};0"
    if lag > CRIT_S:
        print(f"PG_LAG CRITICAL - replay lag {lag} s|{perf}"); sys.exit(2)
    if lag > WARN_S:
        print(f"PG_LAG WARNING - replay lag {lag} s|{perf}"); sys.exit(1)
    print(f"PG_LAG OK - replay lag {lag} s|{perf}"); sys.exit(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
